Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation and clear use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Goal: determine whether an open-model baseline can meet PayGrid's fraud-detection quality thresholds vs your proprietary model (your parity target: >= 95% of baseline F1 on the eval set).
- Redwood suggested experiments:
  1) Run the PayGrid prompt set (attached) against two open models (LlamaX-13B-quant, Orion-7B-fp16) + Redwood-verified optimized kernel paths.
  2) Produce token-level latency/throughput and aggregated F1/precision/recall on your benchmark.
  3) Evaluate cost delta and quantization tradeoffs for the 99th-percentile runtime.

Requested deliverables by Redwood (proposed timeline):
- Day 0: Receive canonical prompt set + sample labels (you to share)
- Day 3: Redwood runs baseline open-model eval and shares benchmarks + prompt-level failure cases
- Day 5: Joint call to review parity results and decide on rollout / additional tuning

I've attached a prompt CSV to get started (paygrid_eval_prompts.csv). If that timeline looks good, we'll kick off on Thursday.

Next steps for you: please confirm the dataset share mechanism (Drive link or S3) and whether we can use the 10k-row seed sample for initial run.

Thanks,

Thanks Lauren — that timeline works for us. A couple of clarifying items: 

1) Parity: yes, our internal bar is 95% F1 vs the proprietary baseline on the seeded eval set. If an open model hits 95+ we can consider a pilot.
2) Data share: we can provide an S3 presigned link to a 10k sample of labeled transactions. I'll share that link by EOD today.
3) Runtime SLOs: our production 99th-percentile latency target for inference is 120 ms per request at typical QPS (burst to 200). We want per-model latency numbers at both median and 99p.

Also: are you planning to run any temperature/decoding/response-length sensitivity sweeps? Some of our prompts are length-sensitive.

—Samir

> I've started the run on our side — attaching the prompt set I used and a short benchmarks deck with model caveats.

Folks — sharing the interim results from the initial run we kicked off overnight. High-level: 

- LlamaX-13B-quant: F1 = 91.8% (vs PayGrid baseline 100% reference), precision 93.5%, recall 90.2%. Latency p99 = 180ms (on our reserved rtx-a100-equivalent pool, quantized path).
- Orion-7B-fp16: F1 = 94.6%, precision 95.1%, recall 94.1%. Latency p99 = 135ms (fp16 path).

Observations:
- Orion-7B-fp16 is closer to parity but still ~0.4 F1 points short of PayGrid's 95% threshold.
- LlamaX-13B-quant shows the biggest cost savings (approx -45% cost vs fp16) but a larger drop in recall on longer prompts (we can share prompt-level failures attached).
- For latency: both models meet median latency targets, but only Orion at fp16 is close to your 99p SLO; LlamaX quantized exceeds it in high-concurrency runs.

Attachments: eval_summary.csv (detailed metrics by prompt + failure examples).

Recommendations / next steps: 
1) Run a targeted prompt-level tuning pass on Orion (prompt engineering + light fine-tune / LoRA on a 5k-sample) — should close the remaining 0.4 F1 gap in most cases.
2) If cost is primary, evaluate hybrid routing: use LlamaX-13B-quant for low-risk transaction types and Orion-fp16 for high-risk ones.
3) Joint call to walk the failure cases and decide pilot scope.

I'll be available for a review call Mon/Tue next week — happy to walk the spreadsheet.

-Marissa
